newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO to firm, tracks healthy paper level.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO to firm, tracks healthy paper level.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were expected to continue its climb on Monday in line with firm paper levels, traders said.
In the paper market, September was bid/asked at $105/$106 a tonne, up from Friday's quotes of $104/$105.
On Friday, 180 cst physical fuel oil was quoted at $104.50/$106 per tonne.
A local trader, previously believed to be short on fuel oil, said he will be interested to sell if the bids were "right".

Some traders said prices will firm up as the trading firm that was said to have won Thailand's recent spot purchase tender was still pricing in his cargoes. But others said the market is still groping for direction as London's International Petroleum Exchange was closed.
Traders said physical fundamentals were balanced. They said while there were limited supplies, demand from China, India and Thailand were also limited.
Late last week, 20,000 tonnes of 180 cst was heard sold to China at $104 per tonne c+f southern China. But traders considered the price to be too low.
